papers.title: Bogoliubov self-consistent $GW$ and second-order Green's function methods for attractive fermionic interactions
papers.abstract: Describing fermionic systems with attractive interactions, such as superconductors and atomic nuclei, beyond the mean-field level remains a central challenge. In this work, we investigate the performance of Bogoliubov fully self-consistent $GW$ (Bog.~sc$GW$) and second-order Green's function (Bog.~scGF2) methods, implemented within a unified imaginary-time and imaginary-frequency framework. Using two attractive Hubbard lattices ($4\times4$ and $2\times8$) as a model study and benchmarking against full configuration interaction (FCI), we find that, for these systems, Bog.~scGF2 provides a more accurate description than Bog.~sc$GW$. In particular, Bog.~sc$GW$ systematically overestimates the correlation energy, with errors increasing rapidly as the attractive interaction strength grows. These results suggest the importance of exchange contributions in such strongly correlated fermionic systems, even when exchange effects are included only at low order in perturbation theory.

papers.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
papers.abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

papers.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
papers.abstract: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $\rho$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.

papers.title: Radii of Sn Isotopes near the Proton Dripline from Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory
papers.abstract: We present the first $\textit{ab initio}$ lattice calculations of charge and matter radii of tin isotopes $^{96}$Sn, $^{98}$Sn, $^{100}$Sn, $^{102}$Sn and $^{104}$Sn near the proton dripline using nuclear lattice effective field theory with high-fidelity two- and three-nucleon forces combined with the partial-pinhole algorithm. The resulting radii are larger then predicted from other ab-initio methods. We find that variations of the three-nucleon interaction reveal substantial radius differences even among interactions with similar binding energies. We intensively discuss of the role of different choices of the three-body forces.

papers.title: Three-nucleon potentials and their matrix elements for $\delta_{\mathrm{NS}}$ in superallowed $\beta$ decays
papers.abstract: We derive three-nucleon potentials for radiative corrections at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ in chiral effective field theory where $\alpha$ is the electromagnetic coupling and $\epsilon_\chi$ is the chiral expansion parameter. These corrections contribute to the nuclear-structure-dependent term $\delta_\mathrm{NS}$ for determinations of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $V_{ud}$ from superallowed nuclear $\beta$ decays. We compute matrix elements of three-nucleon contributions at orders $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ using quantum Monte Carlo methods. We find the matrix elements at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ to be large and to have an effect on the extraction of $V_{ud}$ at the scale of $10^{-4}$. In the case of $^{10}$C, the matrix elements of $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ three-nucleon operators provide a 2% correction to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$, and are thus beyond the current precision goals. The relative size of three-nucleon corrections to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$ in medium mass nuclei, where two-body contributions tend to be smaller, remains to be investigated. We then use these results to determine $V_{ud}$ from the superallowed transition ${}^{10}\mathrm{C}\rightarrow{}^{10}\mathrm{B}$.

papers.title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
papers.abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $\mu_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $\mu_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $\Delta$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $\Xi^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $\mu_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

papers.title: Isospin effects and symmetry energy in nuclear reactions
papers.abstract: Isospin and the symmetry energy are linked within the symmetry term of the liquid-drop mass formula and within the corresponding term of the equation of state of asymmetric nuclear matter. The Pauli exclusion principle leads to a leading quadratic dependence of the kinetic part of the symmetry term of the nuclear binding-energy formula on the neutron-proton asymmetry (N-Z)/A. Charge symmetry ensures the same leading quadratic dependence for the potential part. Charge invariance further generalizes this dependence, to lowest order, from T$_3^2$ to T(T+1). The strength of the symmetry term, in contrast, is determined by the symmetry energy. At sub-saturation densities the symmetry energy can be constrained by nuclear-structure observables, such as neutron skin thicknesses, isovector collective modes and the related electric dipole polarizability, and excitation energies of isobaric analog states. It can also be constrained by reaction observables, such as charge exchange and elastic scattering cross sections, isoscaling and isospin diffusion. At supra-saturation densities, by contrast, the only means of studying asymmetric nuclear matter under laboratory conditions are relativistic heavy-ion collisions. These studies use differential observables such as neutron/proton flows and light isobar or $\pi^{-}/\pi^{+}$ ratios. Complementary information can be obtained from neutron star observations including gravitational waves. The latest measurements and analyses of the stiffness of the symmetry energy will be presented, together with the recent NA61/SHINE observation of an unexpectedly large isospin-symmetry violation in kaon production. Attention will also be paid to the challenges of measuring charged and neutral products of relativistic heavy-ion collisions in the context of the recent ASY-EOS II experiment at GSI and to the new detectors used in the setup.

papers.title: Effects of charm-strange resonances on charmed meson production by recombination in relativistic heavy ion collisions
papers.abstract: We discuss charmed mesons in heavy-ion collisions by focusing on their production from the quark-gluon plasma by quark recombination. We consider the production of not only the $D$, $D^*$, $D_s$, and $D_s^*$, but also the $D_{s0}^*(2317)$, $D_{s1}(2460)$, $D_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_{s2}^*(2573)$, thereby investigating the important role of heavier charm-strange resonances in understanding the measurements of the $D$ and $D_s$ mesons at the Large Hadron Collider at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV. We calculate their yields and transverse momentum distributions, and also evaluate ratios of the transverse momentum distribution between various charmed mesons, i.e., the $D_s$ and $D^0$, the $D_s$ and $D^+$, $D_s^*$ and $D^{*0}$, and $D_s^*$ and $D^{*+}$. Through this analysis, we attempt to understand in more detail the effects of strangeness enhancement on charmed meson production in heavy-ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV.

papers.title: Density functional theory of renormalization group in nuclear matter
papers.abstract: We present the density functional renormalization group (density-fRG), in which density fluctuations are separated from the quantum fluctuations in the vacuum and are integrated out successively within the functional renormalization group approach. This allows us to quantify medium effects and to study the physics of high baryon densities. The method is applied to the nucleon-meson effective field theory, also known as the Walecka model, where the density dependence of the nucleon-meson Yukawa couplings is generated self-consistently by their flow equations. It is found that both the attractive and the repulsive nucleon-meson interactions are screened by the dense medium. This results in an equation of state of symmetric nuclear matter that is stiffer than in the relativistic mean-field approximation for $\rho_0\lesssim\rho\lesssim 2.5\,\rho_0$, and becomes softer for $\rho\gtrsim 2.5\,\rho_0$, where $\rho_0$ is the saturation density. Furthermore, a new phenomenon called the locking of the Fermi surface is found: the effective energy of the quasi-nucleon stays close to the Fermi surface, while both are running with the renormalization group scale.

papers.title: $\Lambda$-deuteron scattering below the $\Sigma$-threshold
papers.abstract: $\Lambda d$ elastic scattering and breakup below the $\Sigma$ threshold is described fully including the virtual coupling to $\Sigma$ channels. Well-converged results are obtained solving the multichannel scattering equations for three-body transition operators in momentum-space. Scattering length, exclusive, semi-inclusive and total elastic and breakup cross sections, and spin observables are calculated, aiming to study their dependence on kinematic variables and dynamic ingredients. The uncertainty due to the hyperon-nucleon interaction model is most sizable. The observables and regimes that could help to constrain the hyperon-nucleon force models are identified. The single-channel approximation of the problem is validated at low and intermediate energies.

papers.title: Predicted Exotic Doubly Heavy-Strange Pentaquarks
papers.abstract: We predict exotic doubly heavy--strange pentaquarks with minimal quark content $u\bar d sQQ'$ ($QQ'=cc,bc,bb$) within a coupled-channel unitary framework where the interaction is derived from an extension of the local hidden gauge approach to the heavy-quark sector. We obtain a robust spectrum of manifestly exotic states; two states appear in the $u\bar d scc$ sector, three in $u\bar d scb$, and two in $u\bar d sbb$. These emerge either as bound states or resonances, along with seven additional virtual states manifested as threshold cusps. The binding mechanism is dominated by off-diagonal transitions among heavy-baryon--light-meson channels, while diagonal interactions are strongly suppressed. These results extend exotic hadron spectroscopy into the doubly heavy--strange sector and provide concrete targets for future experimental searches.

papers.title: Lepton $g-2$ non-universality of hadronic contributions and a sub-GeV window to New Physics
papers.abstract: We propose the linear combination of the anomalous magnetic moments of the muon and electron, $a_{\mu-e} \equiv a_\mu - (m_\mu/m_e)^2 a_e$, as a natural low-energy window quantity that may directly probe the current discrepancy between the data-driven and lattice-QCD evaluations of hadronic contributions. The rescaling ensures an exact cancellation of the leading short-range ($m_\ell^2$-scaling) effects, thereby improving the UV behavior. Because entire classes of contributions cancel identically --- not merely in variance --- the combination is predictable in chiral perturbation theory with no free low-energy constant, and it isolates flavor-non-universal New Physics. The hadronic-vacuum-polarization effect in $a^{\rm HVP}_{\mu-e}$, together with its uncertainty, is reduced as compared to $a^{\rm HVP}_{\mu}$ by $\sim 85\%$. This is promising for tests of New Physics with some degree of flavor non-universality, conditional on significant improvements in the measurements of $a_e$ and $\alpha$.

papers.title: Spin-dependent fermion potentials from mixed tensor couplings of massive spin-1 and spin-2 bosons
papers.abstract: Searches for weak spin-dependent forces are commonly interpreted in terms of a basis of sixteen rotationally invariant two-fermion potentials. We derive finite-range coordinate-space potentials generated by a massive spin-1 boson with vector, axial-vector, tensor, and pseudotensor couplings to Dirac fermions. In addition to the familiar vector--vector, vector--axial-vector, and axial-vector--axial-vector interactions, we obtain the mixed vector--tensor, vector--pseudotensor, axial-vector--tensor, and axial-vector--pseudotensor potentials, together with tensor--tensor, tensor--pseudotensor, and pseudotensor--pseudotensor terms. We retain the contact terms needed in atomic-scale applications and give compact expressions that include both orderings of inequivalent fermion vertices. We then extend the analysis to a massive spin-2 mediator described by a symmetric Fierz--Pauli field. Besides the conventional coupling to the conserved fermion energy--momentum tensor, we consider a symmetric axial-tensor current. Its nonconservation for massive fermions makes the longitudinal spin-2 helicities contribute to axial-tensor--axial-tensor exchange. The leading minimal spin-2 interactions are either P,T even or P odd and T evenl. Heavy-mediator contact limits and the distinction between the M-->0 massive-spin-2 limit and a genuine massless graviton are also discussed. We map the resulting interactions onto the sixteen-potential Dobrescu--Mocioiu basis and use this mapping to translate existing experimental constraints into numerical limits on spin-1 and spin-2 coupling products in the small- and large-mediator-mass regimes, together with representative limits at finite mediator masses. The derived relations between the boson-exchange coupling constants and the coefficients of the basis potentials also allow published exclusion curves to be rescaled to arbitrary mediator masses.
